title: Gascony's Legacy - a tactical skirmish game set in the fiction of Alexandre Dumas
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V50CUypS7UM

After the middling Red Sonja and the beloved Avalon's Legacy, which leapt into his top ten, Daniel (@dungeondive) moves on to Lynnvander's Gascony's Legacy, a cooperative tactical skirmish game set in Dumas's Three Musketeers. He picked up the base game, both story expansions (The Man in the Iron Mask and The Count of Monte Cristo) and the 3D terrain for about $50 on eBay, and calls that a steal.

The "campaign" is really a set of standalone, lightly branching acts told through numbered story cards. Combat is the whole show, and it's excellent. Facing matters, which is rare: stance tokens on the standees fix which hand holds which weapon, and every weapon has its own attack arc (a pike reaches two squares ahead, a stiletto only one). The star is the enemy reaction deck. Whenever you wound but don't kill a foe, it might dodge, counter, call for help or slip around you out of your arc. Fights become a constantly shifting, choreographed dance, unlike the stand-and-roll slugfests of Warhammer Quest.

He demonstrates a turn at the Duke of Buckingham's party: d'Artagnan and Aramis hunt for the right exit, after he had already kicked a flaming brazier onto the Cardinal's Captain. Terrain is everywhere, from tables to leap onto, barrels to roll and haystacks to hide in. Shared Stones of Destiny, simple enemies and named villains (Richelieu, Milady de Winter, Rochefort) round it out. It's not a lifestyle game, but it's cheap, quick and fun. Buffy is next.

----

Which game has given you the most dynamic, choreographed-feeling combat, where positioning mattered as much as dice?
